synthesis.description: Customers, suppliers and internal desks send daily and monthly gas nominations: Calpine and Enron Methanol send standing daily nomination documents, a pipeline system sends its nomination, and plant and producer contacts send revised volumes when production drops or demand changes. Schedulers and logistics staff enter the volumes in Sitara and on the pipeline, set up the month's estimates, rework deal tickets and meters when a party revises its request, and confirm the change back.
steps: A customer, supplier or desk sends a daily or monthly nomination, or an estimate for the coming month.
The scheduler checks the volumes against the deal, meter and transport contract.
The scheduler enters or updates the volumes in Sitara and nominates them on the pipeline.
When a party revises its volumes, the scheduler updates the setup, deal ticket or meter, sometimes retroactively.
Missing transport numbers or contract details are chased with the counterparty or other desks.
The scheduler confirms the nomination is entered, tracked and balanced.
synthesis.approach: Parse the standing daily nomination documents and revision emails into a structured feed that pre-fills Sitara and pipeline nominations, flags changes against the prior day or month setup, and lists missing transport numbers or contracts for the scheduler to resolve.
synthesis.rationale: Most rounds are routine re-entry of volumes from standing documents, and the stalls come from missed checks (wrong setups, missing transport, protected tickets); a nomination checklist covering volume, meter, contract and transport before entry would cut rework tomorrow.
